name: נְתַנְאֵל
summary: Borne first by Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar in the wilderness, who stood with Moses at the numbering, brought Issachar's offering on the second day and led its host when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 1:8; 7:18; 10:15); then by David's brother, by priests who blew trumpets before the ark, by a Levite scribe's father, a son of Obed-edom, one of Jehoshaphat's princes sent to teach the law, a chief Levite under Josiah, and priests and singers of the return; and in the New Testament by Nathanael of Cana, “an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile” (Jhn 1:47). It joins the perfect נָתַן, “has given”, to אֵל, God: “God has given”, the same sentence as נְתַנְיָהוּ, “Yahweh has given”, and as Phoenician ytnʾl. Leah used the same verb when she named Issachar, Nethanel's forefather: “God has given (נָתַן) my hire” (Gen 30:18).

evidence.note: Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Issachar, נְתַנְאֵל בֶּן־צוּעָר.
For Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar, among the men who stood with Moses and Aaron.
The leader of the sons of Issachar, camped beside Judah on the east.
On the second day Nethanel brought Issachar's offering (to 7:23).
Nethanel, the fourth son of Jesse.
Among the priests blowing the trumpets before the ark of God.
Shemaiah son of Nethanel, the Levite scribe.
Nethanel, the fifth son of Obed-edom.
One of the princes Jehoshaphat sent to teach in the cities of Judah.
Among the chiefs of the Levites who gave Passover offerings under Josiah.
Of the sons of Pashhur, among those who had taken foreign wives.
Head of the priestly house of Jedaiah in Joiakim's days.
Among the musicians at the dedication of the wall.
Philip finds Ναθαναήλ: “we have found him of whom Moses in the law and the prophets wrote”; also Jhn 1:47–49; 21:2.
Leah: “God has given (נָתַן אֱלֹהִים) my hire”, and she called his name Issachar: the verb and the subject of the name, in the naming of Nethanel's tribe.
“Yahweh נָתַן”: the perfect with God as its subject, as in the name.
Phoenician-Punic “YATON-ʾIL (‘Il/God give/gave’)”: the same name in the Phoenician form of the verb.

note: BDB key n.gg.ae (Num 1:8; 2:5; 7:18, 23; 10:15; 1Ch 2:14; 15:24; 24:6; 26:4; 2Ch 17:7; 35:9; Ezr 10:22; Neh 12:21, 36). Abbott-Smith gives Ναθαναήλ as the Hebrew נְתַנְאֵל, so TIPNR's Nathanael@Jhn.1.45 is included as a bearer of the same name, as Gamaliel@Act.5.34 is under gamaliel. 1Ch 15:24 and 1Ch 26:4 may be one man (both with Obed-edom in David's day); TIPNR keeps them apart and so does this entry. Related names of the root not drafted here: נְתַנְיָהוּ “Yahweh has given”, נָתָן, מַתַּנְיָהוּ, מַתִּתְיָהוּ.
